- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast by 1–3% for days 1–5 post-spike.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods; if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture rebound.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns positive after day 15, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for days 16–30.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -1.0 → +1.0), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for day 20–30 to capture momentum.
